what: The table summarises 31 repeat tests of one chemical (M2CA) on light-emitting bacteria. For each measure of toxicity at 15, 30 and 45 minutes it gives the average, the spread (standard deviation, coefficient of variation, range) and a test of whether the values look normally distributed.
verdict: Yes: 91 of 95 cells were rebuilt within 2% by both runs, and the other 4 are within 6% and trace to the published table itself or to rounding, not to the method.
verdict_note: Two printed values do not follow from the authors' own deposited per-test results: one mean is very likely a typo, and one CV cannot be obtained from the data. The other two misses sit on a rounding boundary and match once the per-test values are rounded the way the authors report them.
implication: The Methods were good enough to rebuild the table from raw data. A check that each printed mean, SD and CV agree with each other (SD / mean x 100 = CV) would have caught the one clear typo before publication.
model_note: The two runs made the same choices (same 31 tests, duplicates fitted as separate points, n-1 SD, range as max minus min) and got the same numbers to about six digits, so they missed the same four cells. With one run per model, this says nothing about a difference between the models.

causes.title: Printed mean for s at 30 minutes is a likely typo
causes.left_unsaid: The table prints a mean of 0.55 for the asymmetry value s at 30 minutes, but its own SD (0.084) and CV (15.7%) imply a mean of 0.535, and the authors' own deposited per-test values average 0.535.

ai_did.r_opus: Fitted all 31 tests and averaged s at 30 min: 0.535 (prints as 0.53).
ai_did.r_sonnet: Same fits and the same average: 0.535.

causes.authors_did: Their deposited per-test s values give 0.535; the 0.55 in the table is most likely a typing slip for 0.53 or 0.535.
causes.fix: Correct the mean of s at 30 minutes to 0.53 (0.535).
causes.evidence: The authors' supplement values give mean 0.5347, SD 0.0837, CV 15.66%, matching the printed SD and CV; 0.084 / 0.157 = 0.535, while 0.084 / 0.55 would give CV 15.3%, not the printed 15.7. No drop-one subset gets above 0.539.

example.alternative: 0.535 (authors' own per-test values; no reading gives 0.55)

causes.title: Printed CV of r2 at 15 minutes not supported by the data
causes.left_unsaid: The table prints a CV of 0.17% for the fit quality r2 (how well each curve fits, 1 = perfect) at 15 minutes. The authors' own deposited per-test r2 values give 0.164%, which prints as 0.16.

ai_did.r_opus: Computed CV from its 31 fitted r2 values: 0.164%.

causes.authors_did: Unknown. Their deposited r2 values reproduce the runs' 0.164, not 0.17.
causes.fix: Correct the CV of r2 at 15 minutes to 0.16, or state how it was computed.
causes.evidence: Authors' supplement values: mean 0.99771, SD 0.001637, CV 0.164% (same as the runs). Population SD gives 0.161. Rounding each r2 to 3 decimals first gives 0.169 (prints 0.17), but that same rounding breaks the 30-minute row (Shapiro-Wilk W 0.68 instead of the printed 0.830), so it is not a consistent procedure.

example.alternative: 0.164 (authors' own values); 0.169 only with r2 rounded to 3 decimals, which breaks other rows

causes.title: Small rounding differences at a rounding boundary
causes.left_unsaid: The Methods do not say that per-test values were rounded (to the precision printed in the supplement) before the summary statistics were taken. Both cells sit just below a rounding boundary, so this tiny step flips the last printed digit.

ai_did.r_opus: Used unrounded fitted values: range of s at 30 min 0.3345 (prints 0.33); CV of r2 at 45 min 0.0545 (prints 0.05).

causes.authors_did: Evidently worked from rounded per-test values: their largest and smallest s at 30 min are 0.7476 and 0.4131, which as 0.75 and 0.41 give a range of 0.34; their r2 values are reported to 4 decimals.
causes.fix: State that summary statistics were computed from per-test values rounded to the decimals shown in the supplementary table.
causes.evidence: Taking the range from values rounded to the printed decimals gives 0.34 for s at 30 min and keeps all 18 range cells within 2% for the run values. Rounding the runs' per-test r2 to 4 decimals moves the 45-minute CV from 0.0545 to 0.0551 (prints 0.06, the published value); the authors' own values give 0.057.

notes: The two runs chose the same 31 tests as the authors: the M2CA-alone test of all 30 combinations plus the second M2CA test of the sham M2CA-M2CA combination. The authors' supplement confirms this.
The runs' per-test fits match the authors' deposited values to 4 decimals for every test except two 45-minute curves (M2CA-4NBB, M2CA-EUG), where the runs found slightly better-fitting curves.
For M2CA-4NBB at 45 min the authors list r2 = 0.9982, but their own listed parameters give r2 = 0.9991 on the deposited raw data, so that printed r2 does not follow from their own fit.
The printed SD values for r2 (0.002, 0.001, 0.001) are rounded too coarsely to recompute the printed CVs from them (0.002 / 0.9977 = 0.20, not 0.17).
